children.game_version: The 'Umbrella Game' where children take turns being the queen and processing under a makeshift umbrella.

seniors.seated_version: Perform the rhythmic arm movements and vocal responses while seated; use hand-held bells to mimic the ogene pulse.
seniors.standing_version: Slow-tempo processional walking with a focus on posture rather than vigorous footwork.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduce tempo by 30%; limit the range of waist and hip swaying.

social_formats.description: The dance is performed by a group led by a chief vocalist (Queen) and supported by instrumentalists and backup dancers.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: The queen holds a horsetail and a bronze staff; dancers use arm movements to complement the raffia shrouds
movement_profile.footwork: Rhythmic stepping that activates calf and ankle jingles
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Processional entry followed by a stage-based group display
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Movement is accentuated by ten strings of beads at the waist and raffia shrouds
movement_profile.partnering: None; group-based with a central lead
movement_profile.posture: Upright and regal for the queen; energetic and rhythmic for the dancers

signature_moves.description: A slow, majestic walk under a large umbrella accompanied by fanning
signature_moves.name: The Queen's Entrance

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Matches the driving beat of the ogene
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid stepping out of sync with the ogene beat; ensure the heavy bronze crown is balanced

music_profile.musical_form: Introductory flute solo followed by vocal-led rhythmic sections
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Dependent on the beat of the ogene metal gong
music_profile.sound_description: The sound is defined by the sharp, resonant clanging of the ogene metal gong and the melodic, breathy calls of the flute. It features a call-and-response vocal structure led by a powerful female voice, supported by the deep earthy tones of the udu and ekwe drums.
music_profile.vocal_style: Chief vocalist (Queen) with backup singers; lyrics address social issues

basic_steps: Wait for the flute cue to begin the entrance procession
Processional walk following the queen under the umbrella
Rhythmic stepping synchronized with the ogene gong beat
Vocal response to the lead singer's call
Coordinated movement of calf and ankle jingles during footwork
teaching.formation: Processional entrance leading to a stage performance centered around a lead vocalist
teaching.level_notes: Requires high stamina for rhythmic stepping and the ability to carry heavy beaded costumes.
teaching.rhythm: Percussive and steady, driven by the metal ogene gong
